newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI OUT FOR TWO MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI OUT FOR TWO MONTHS.

text.p: Brazilian Christian Fittipaldi will be unable to drive for at least two months after breaking his leg on Sunday in a high-speed crash, an Australian IndyCar spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Fittipaldi, who broke his right leg in two places in a spectacular crash during the street circuit race at Queensland's Surfers' Paradise on Sunday, was "stable and comfortable" in a local hospital.
A steel rod 360mm (14 inches) long was inserted into the leg during three-hour corrective surgery on the tibia bone on Sunday night, IndyCar Australia spokeswoman Nan Dwyer said.
"Christian will be out of racing for at least two months. I don't think he will be able to drive at all during that time," Dwyer added.
"He is hopeful he will be able to leave Australia before the end of the week."
Fittipaldi was injured in a crash at the end of the first lap, forcing a restart of the race, which was won by American driver Scott Pruett.
The crash occured when Fittipaldi's Swift Ford appeared to be bumped from behind in a chicane leading to the main straight and smashed into a side wall, sending debris flying in all directions.
His car was travelling at more than 240 km (150 miles per hour) at the moment of impact and travelled another 400 metres (yards) along the track before coming to a halt.

The Brazilian is the nephew of former IndyCar and Formula One drivers' champion Emerson Fittipaldi, who himself underwent a five-hour operation to repair a fracture of the vertebra after a high-speed race crash last July.
